answers.q1: Bundler with Rake (Ruby gems). Run `bundle install` from the repo root. The sub-projects have their own Gemfiles, so also run `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install)` and `(cd rack-protection && bundle install)`.
answers.q2: `bundle exec rake && (cd rack-protection && bundle exec rake) && (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake)`. The root `bundle exec rake` runs the default `test` task (Minitest). The other two run the sub-gem suites, matching the CI steps in .github/workflows/test.yml.
answers.q3: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb)`. It must run from sinatra-contrib because rspec is only in sinatra-contrib/Gemfile, not the root Gemfile.
answers.q4: CI runs no lint or formatting check. .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml contain no rubocop step. The repo does ship a RuboCop config (.rubocop.yml, with rubocop ~> 1.32.0 in the root Gemfile), so the closest local check is `bundle exec rubocop` from the repo root.
answers.q5: None are marked as do-not-edit. Build output and vendored paths (vendor/, doc/, coverage/, pkg/, *.gem, *.lock) are git-ignored per .gitignore. sinatra-contrib/sinatra-contrib.gemspec is rewritten by `rake gemspec` (author, email and file fields come from git), and the lib/**/version.rb files are rewritten by the release:commit_version task, so edit those only through those tasks. I did not check whether the root sinatra.gemspec is also generated.

q1.reason: Gives `bundle install` from the root, plus the sub-project installs, which is harmless extra detail.

q2.reason: Includes root `bundle exec rake` and the sub-gem runs matching CI, with no contradiction of the truth.

q3.reason: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb)` matches the accepted command.

q4.reason: Says CI runs no linter and gives `bundle exec rubocop` as the local check, matching the accepted answer.

q5.reason: Says none are marked do-not-edit and mentions coverage/ and doc/ as ignored output, but also claims generated gemspec and version.rb files that the truth does not support, and admits uncertainty.
